name: Robinhood
rootCause: The Robinhood Twitter account was hacked and used to promote a fraudulent crypto project. The hackers announced the launch of a new token called $RBH, which they say will be priced at $0.0005 on Binance Smart Chain. About 25 people purchased the fraudulent tokens for a total of just under $8,000 before the link was removed. Robinhood said in a blog post that the unauthorized content posted on Robinhood Twitter, Instagram and Facebook was removed within minutes, and the team believes the source of the incident was a third-party vendor.

descriptions.text: The Robinhood Twitter account was hacked and used to promote a fraudulent crypto project. The hackers announced the launch of a new token called $RBH, which they say will be priced at $0.0005 on Binance Smart Chain. About 25 people purchased the fraudulent tokens for a total of just under $8,000 before the link was removed. Robinhood said in a blog post that the unauthorized content posted on Robinhood Twitter, Instagram and Facebook was removed within minutes, and the team believes the source of the incident was a third-party vendor.

Robinhood's official social media accounts were compromised on January 25, 2023. The attacker promoted a fraudulent RBH token on BNB Chain, luring victims to purchase it via PancakeSwap. Estimated losses range from $8,200 to $16,000 in BNB. Binance quickly intervened, freezing related accounts and removing posts. The root cause was social engineering through a third-party vendor controlling Robinhood's social access. The incident was caused by social engineering targeting a third-party vendor controlling Robinhood's social media accounts. This allowed the attacker to broadcast scam token promotions, resulting in user losses. No on-chain contract vulnerability or protocol flaw was involved.
